\chapter{Boolean Analysis — LMN Concentration}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.LMN.LMNConcentration
\section{Overview}

This module composes the two halves of the Linial--Mansour--Nisan argument: the
multi-switching collapse of a bounded-depth circuit to a shallow decision tree under a
Bernoulli-random restriction, and the transfer from likely shallowness under restriction
to Fourier concentration. The result is that a circuit of depth $d$, size $s$, and
fan-in $w$ has its Fourier spectrum $4\varepsilon$-concentrated --- up to Chernoff tail
terms vanishing as $n \to \infty$ --- below degree
$O\!\left(w \log(s/\varepsilon)^{d-2} \log(1/\varepsilon)\right)$.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[LMN Fourier concentration, parametric form]
\lean{RestrictionFourier.circuit_fourier_concentration}
\label{RestrictionFourier.circuit_fourier_concentration}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.Circuit, BoolCircuit.Circuit.depth, BoolCircuit.Circuit.eval, BoolCircuit.Circuit.maxFanin, BoolCircuit.Circuit.size, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, LMN.composedDelta, LMN.composedDelta_le_one, LMN.composedDelta_pos, LMN.odonnell_lemma_4_28, RestrictionFourier.odonnell_lemma_4_21, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb, SwitchingLemma2.restrictFn, dtDepth}
\difficulty{4}
Let $C$ be a Boolean circuit on $n \ge 1$ input bits with depth at most $d$, size at
most $s$, and gate fan-in at most $w$, where $d \ge 2$ and $s, w \ge 1$. Let $l \ge 1$
and $t$ be natural numbers, and let $\varepsilon > 0$ be a real number such that the
switching parameters satisfy $s \cdot 2^{-l} \le \varepsilon/2$ and
$2^{-t} \le \varepsilon/2$. Write
$\delta = \frac{1}{40w}\bigl(\frac{1}{40l}\bigr)^{d-2}$ for the composed restriction
rate, $\sigma$ for the sign encoding of a bit ($\sigma(\mathtt{false}) = 1$,
$\sigma(\mathtt{true}) = -1$), and $\widehat{\sigma \circ C}(U)$ for the Fourier--Walsh
coefficient at $U \subseteq [n]$ of the $\pm1$-encoding of the function computed by $C$.
Then the Fourier weight above degree $3(t+1)/\delta$ is small:
\[
  \sum_{\substack{U \subseteq [n] \\ 3(t+1) \le \delta\,\abs{U}}}
    \widehat{\sigma \circ C}(U)^2
  \;\le\;
  4\left(\varepsilon + s\,e^{-n/(120 w)} + s\,e^{-n/(120 l)}\right).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[The concentration threshold in explicit form]
\lean{RestrictionFourier.composedDelta_mul_card_iff}
\label{RestrictionFourier.composedDelta_mul_card_iff}
\leanok
\uses{LMN.composedDelta}
\difficulty{3}
Let $w \ge 1$, $l \ge 1$, and $d$ be natural numbers, let $a$ be a real number, and let
$m$ be a natural number. Writing
$\delta = \frac{1}{40w}\bigl(\frac{1}{40l}\bigr)^{d-2}$, where the exponent $d-2$ is
taken to be $0$ when $d \le 2$, the inequality $a \le \delta m$ holds if and only if
\[
  a \cdot 40 w \, (40 l)^{d-2} \;\le\; m.
\]
(Taking $a = 3(t+1)$ with $t \approx \log_2(1/\varepsilon)$ and
$l \approx \log_2(s/\varepsilon)$, this exhibits the LMN degree threshold as
$O\!\left(w \log(s/\varepsilon)^{d-2} \log(1/\varepsilon)\right)$.)
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[LMN Fourier concentration at logarithmic degree]
\lean{RestrictionFourier.circuit_fourier_concentration_log}
\label{RestrictionFourier.circuit_fourier_concentration_log}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.Circuit, BoolCircuit.Circuit.depth, BoolCircuit.Circuit.eval, BoolCircuit.Circuit.maxFanin, BoolCircuit.Circuit.size, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, LMN.composedDelta, LMN.logb_2s_div_eps_pos, LMN.size_times_two_pow_neg_l_le, LMN.two_pow_neg_logb_2_div_eps, RestrictionFourier.circuit_fourier_concentration}
\difficulty{4}
Let $C$ be a Boolean circuit on $n \ge 1$ input bits with depth at most $d$, size at
most $s$, and gate fan-in at most $w$, where $d \ge 2$ and $s, w \ge 1$, and let
$\varepsilon$ be a real number with $0 < \varepsilon \le 1$. Set
$l = \lceil \log_2(2s/\varepsilon) \rceil$ and $t = \lceil \log_2(2/\varepsilon) \rceil$,
and write $\delta = \frac{1}{40w}\bigl(\frac{1}{40l}\bigr)^{d-2}$, $\sigma$ for the
sign encoding of a bit ($\sigma(\mathtt{false}) = 1$, $\sigma(\mathtt{true}) = -1$),
and $\widehat{\sigma \circ C}(U)$ for the Fourier--Walsh coefficient at
$U \subseteq [n]$ of the $\pm1$-encoding of the function computed by $C$. Then
\[
  \sum_{\substack{U \subseteq [n] \\ 3(t+1) \le \delta\,\abs{U}}}
    \widehat{\sigma \circ C}(U)^2
  \;\le\;
  4\left(\varepsilon + s\,e^{-n/(120 w)} + s\,e^{-n/(120 l)}\right);
\]
that is, the Fourier spectrum of $\sigma \circ C$ is concentrated --- up to Chernoff
tail terms that vanish as $n \to \infty$ --- below degree
$3\bigl(\lceil\log_2(2/\varepsilon)\rceil + 1\bigr) \cdot 40 w \,
\bigl(40\lceil\log_2(2s/\varepsilon)\rceil\bigr)^{d-2}
= O\!\left(w \log(s/\varepsilon)^{d-2} \log(1/\varepsilon)\right)$.
\end{theorem}
